newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Germany denounces Iran "blackmail" on ambassador.
newsitem.headline: Germany denounces Iran "blackmail" on ambassador.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Thursday denounced as improper Iran's refusal to accept the return of its ambassador and said his country would not submit to "blackmail".
"We will not impose our ambassadors on Tehran," Kinkel told a news conference at the close of a two-day visit to Romania. "We Germans won't let ourselves be blackmailed or divided."
Kinkel said he believed statements in Tehran that neither the German and Danish ambassadors were welcome in Tehran were motivated by a European Union decision this week to send the envoys back.
The campaign for the country's May 23 presidential election had also played a role, he said.
"That obviously led the Tehran leadership, which is now in an electoral campaign, to react in this way, which I personally see as totally improper," he said.
He suggested EU countries would not now send their ambassadors back.

"European solidarity will be shown again and for that I am thankful," he said. "We will not allow Iran to continue its election campaign at our cost and we will evaluate the situation after the elections in Iran."

Iranian news media quoted Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati on Wednesday as saying Tehran would not object if the German ambassador did not return and "may even be...pleased". He said the same applied to the ambassador of Denmark, which has been critical of human rights standards in Iran.
The EU initially withdrew its ambassadors earlier this month after a German court implicated senior Iranian officials in the 1992 killing of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
A meeting of EU foreign ministers this week agreed to send the ambassadors back but suspended ministerial contacts.

Kinkel had been a leading proponent of "critical dialogue" with Iran and had led EU efforts to persuade Iran to lift death threats against British author Salman Rushdie over publication of his novel "The Satanic Verses".
After the Iranian statements, the Netherlands as current EU chairman asked member statements not to send their envoys back to Iran.
This would prove to Iran, a Dutch statement said, that the EU was unanimous in rejecting "arbitrary measures against some member states".
But an Italian embassy official in Tehran, speaking by telephone, told Reuters his ambassador had returned.
Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, who is due to be replaced in the election, said Tehran had initiated the suspension of "critical dialogue" before the EU move.
The United States this week welcomed the EU's suspension of dialogue, saying it had been a total failure in trying to persuade Iran to observe human rights commitments.
